# 0.13.0 — vocabulary scoping, validate output, safe CI

12 October 2026. Minor on **0.12.1**.

Four things need action after upgrading. `threat.surface` values are now stage-scoped, so `Windows::Desktop` becomes `OS::Windows::Desktop`. Platform configuration blocks now require `status`. `opentide --json validate --check <x>` returns the same document as a bare `validate`, and its legacy `errors` map is gone. Re-run `opentide setup ci` — generated pipelines previously deployed to the staging tenant and pushed to your default branch from **any** pull request.

## Install

```bash
pip install opentide==0.13.0
export OPENTIDE_REPO_ROOT=/path/to/detection-repo
opentide generate schemas templates vocabs snippets
opentide validate --strict
```

## Breaking

- **`threat.surface` is stage-scoped.** An authored value is `<stage>::<key>`. The vocabulary groups keys under 8 stages and defines the same key under two of them, so a bare key name was ambiguous and five values (`VPN`, `VPN::OpenVPN`, `VPN::WireGuard`, `Wireless`, `Industrial` — each both `Infrastructure` and `Protocol`) were unreachable. The enum carried 895 values where the vocabulary defines 900; it now carries all 900.
- **Platform configuration requires `status`.** A rule missing `configurations.<platform>.status` previously passed `validate`, failed the published JSON Schema, and then crashed the deployer. Validation now reports `status: Field required` with the field path.
- **`opentide --json validate` emits one shape.** The report is always at `report`; `checks` maps each check that ran to its verdict. `--check <x>` narrows `checks` and adds `check` instead of relocating the report to `issues`. The duplicate legacy `errors` map is removed — read `report.issues`.
- **Local vocabulary extension is removed.** The CoreTIDE-era `[vocabulary]` block in `schema.toml` no longer injects entries. Vocabularies are canonical in [specifications](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/specifications); a missing entry is added upstream.

## Fixed

- Generated CI gated staging deployment and default-branch pushes on *"is this a PR"* and never on *"does it target the default branch"* — so a PR between two feature branches deployed detections to a live staging tenant and landed a commit on the default branch. Six jobs across GitLab, GitHub and Azure. Re-run `opentide setup ci`.
- `threat.actors.name` is pinned to `actors::1.1`. 220 threat-actor galaxy clusters were present in the bundled vocabulary but invisible behind the `actors::1.0` pin, so a correctly-authored MISP cluster UUID was reported as an unknown vocabulary value. The actors enum goes from 1029 to 1249 values.
- `opentide setup skills --install opentide-detection-rule` no longer fails as an unknown slug. Three of the four wheel-bundled authoring skills were absent from the discovery catalogue while remaining in the default starter set, so the CLI installed a slug it refused to name.
- The weekly vocabulary refresh workflow had never completed a run since it was introduced: the OpenTide pull-request step was not gated on the App credential the specifications step already required, so it fell back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`, force-pushed the branch, and then failed at `gh pr create`. It now fails fast, before any mutation, with a message naming the missing secrets.

## Verify

```bash
python -c "import opentide; print(opentide.__version__)"
```

Expect `0.13.0`.
